items.context: Documenting ₿itcoin (@DocumentingBTC, 1.121.921 seguidores) pregunta "Who pays the Bitcoin miners?" con un adjunto multimedia. Lleva ~1 h con 31 likes, 12 reposts, 12 respuestas y 6973 vistas, creciendo. Encaja con el tema de halving y emisión: subsidio por bloque y comisiones.
items.suggested_text:
Two sources, and the mix between them is the real story: newly issued coins plus transaction fees. Today the larger share typically comes from issuance, 3.125 BTC per block, roughly 450 BTC a day.

That subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks. At the next halving it drops to 1.5625 BTC, about 225 a day, and only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue. Every cut shifts more of the security budget onto fees, meaning onto the people actually using the chain.

The long-run question isn't whether miners get paid. It's whether demand for blockspace grows fast enough to replace a subsidy that keeps halving toward zero.
